observed_title: Poisson Stochastic Integration in Banach Spaces

read_ranges.scope: 全文逐行阅读：martingale type/cotype estimates, stochastic convolutions, UMD Poisson norm, vector-valued Poisson Malliavin derivative and Skorohod extension, Clark–Ocone projection/formula, all proofs and references.

topic_relevance.K03: adjacent method source only. The paper gives Banach-valued Poisson integral moment/maximal estimates and a stochastic Poisson p-norm; its martingale/Rosenthal estimates can help supply finite-increment controls, but it has no generic chaining, local measure functional, or simultaneous all-index pointwise majorization.
topic_relevance.J04: adjacent integral-calculus source. It rigorously treats compensated Poisson integration, UMD/type-cotype hypotheses, conditional-expectation projections, and a Clark–Ocone representation under a natural Poisson filtration. Its intensity is deterministic and its target is a compensated Poisson random measure, so it does not itself define a nonhomogeneous state-dependent compensator or the exit-settlement interface.

definitions.name: martingale type and cotype
definitions.statement: X has martingale type s∈(1,2] when Ls-moments of any finite X-valued martingale-difference sum are bounded by the ℓs sum of the differences; finite martingale cotype r≥2 gives the reverse square-sum-type control. These geometric assumptions yield one-sided Bichteler–Jacod upper and lower bounds.

definitions.name: Poisson p-norm
definitions.statement: For a simple X-valued f=Σ_j1_{B_j}x_j on disjoint finite-intensity sets, ||f||_{ν_p(E;X)}=(E||Σ_j N~(B_j)x_j||_X^p)^(1/p); the completion is the integrand space for an abstract UMD Poisson Itô isomorphism. This norm is generally stochastic rather than an explicit deterministic function-space norm.

definitions.name: Poisson Malliavin derivative and adapted projection
definitions.statement: For cylindrical F=f(N(B_1),…,N(B_M)) on disjoint finite-intensity sets, D is the finite add-one difference Σ_m[f(N+e_m)−f(N)]1_{B_m}; the predictable projection P_F is the strong operator limit of partitionwise conditional expectation maps in the Poisson p-norm.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.11 and Theorem 2.13 (martingale type upper / cotype lower bounds)
assumptions: X has martingale type s∈(1,2] for Theorem 2.11, or finite martingale cotype s∈[2,∞) for Theorem 2.13.
N is a compensated Poisson random measure with deterministic intensity dt×ν; φ is a simple adapted X-valued process and B is a measurable mark set.
theorem_cards.statement: If X has martingale type s and s≤p<∞, the maximal Lp norm of ∫φdN~ is bounded by ||φ1_B||_{D_{s,X}^p∩D_{p,X}^p}; if 1<p≤s the bound uses D_{s,X}^p+D_{p,X}^p. If X has martingale cotype s and s≤p, the matching intersection integrand norm is bounded by the terminal integral Lp norm; when 1<p<s, the corresponding sum norm is bounded.
proof_steps: Apply Doob to reduce the maximal upper estimate. Refine the elementary time/mark partition until each cell has intensity λ≤1, and order the cells lexicographically to create a filtration. The centered cell counts multiplied by adapted coefficients form a martingale difference sequence.

For type s, combine extrapolation of the martingale type inequality with Lemma 2.6 and the Poisson moment estimate E|N−λ|^r≈_r λ for λ≤1. In the p<s regime, decompose the integrand into the Lp-size and Ls-size components, project onto the partition algebra, and use reverse dual Doob.

For cotype, prove the high-p lower estimate using the cotype extrapolation and small-cell Poisson moment comparison; derive the low-p case by duality. Proofs appear at lines 454–565 and 619–686, pp.8–12.
gaps: These are one-sided results in general Banach spaces and do not characterize the exact integrability norm except in special cases (notably Hilbert spaces).
The Poisson increment moments rely on deterministic-intensity cells and adaptation; no random/state-dependent intensity kernel is addressed.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.3 (maximal inequality for stochastic convolutions)
assumptions: 1<s≤2; X has martingale type s; S is a bounded C0-semigroup with an isometric dilation on a martingale-type-s space Y.
φ is a simple adapted process, B is a mark set; p is in the type-dependent ranges s≤p or 1≤p<s as stated.
theorem_cards.statement: The maximal Lp norm of the Poisson stochastic convolution ∫_(0,t]S(t−u)φ(u)dN~ is bounded by D_{s,X}^p∩D_{p,X}^p for s≤p, and by D_{s,X}^p+D_{p,X}^p in the low-p range.
proof_steps: Use the isometric dilation QS(t−u)=PU(t−u)Q, transfer the supremum to the group U, and commute U(−u) into the integrand. Apply Theorem 2.11 in Y and boundedness of Q/P to return to X. The low-p case follows by decomposing the integrand into two simple adapted parts.
gaps: Requires a semigroup isometric dilation on another martingale-type space; such a dilation is not automatic for every bounded semigroup.
The proof relies on stochastic-integral extension/density from Lemma 3.2 and the type estimate.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4.5 (UMD abstract Poisson Itô isomorphism)
assumptions: X is UMD; 1<p<∞; φ is simple adapted and N is a Poisson random measure with σ-finite deterministic intensity.
theorem_cards.statement: The maximal integral norm (E sup_{t>0}||∫_(0,t] φ dN~||_X^p)^(1/p) is equivalent, with constants depending on p and X, to ||φ||_{L_F^p(Ω;ν_p(R_+×J;X))}; L_F^p is the closure of simple adapted processes in the stochastic Poisson-p norm.
proof_steps: The statement is reduced to the UMD decoupling inequality and Doob maximal inequality; Section 4 identifies explicit deterministic descriptions of ν_p for Hilbert and Lq spaces, while noting the general norm remains stochastic.
gaps: This is an abstract integrability norm, not a deterministic closed-form criterion for general X.
The theorem does not itself identify the compensator of an arbitrary jump process; it assumes a Poisson random measure.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 5.10 (Poisson Skorohod divergence extends adapted Itô integral)
assumptions: X is UMD and 1<p<∞. The filtration is the natural filtration generated by the compensated Poisson random measure.
theorem_cards.statement: Every adapted integrand in L_F^p(Ω;ν_p(R_+×J;X)) belongs to the divergence operator domain and δ(φ)=I(φ); hence the adjoint of the Poisson Malliavin derivative extends the Itô integral on adapted inputs.
proof_steps: For cylindrical elementary adapted integrands use the integration-by-parts identity to show δ(F·1_(a,b]·1_A·x)=F N~((a,b]×A)x=I of that term. Use density of cylindrical F_t-measurable variables, closedness of δ, and closure of simple adapted processes in the ν_p norm.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Theorem 5.10 statement, proof and natural-filtration caveat.

gaps: The natural-filtration condition is explicitly used for density of cylindrical F_s variables; the theorem is not stated for arbitrary larger filtrations.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 6.6 (Clark–Ocone representation)
assumptions: X is UMD and 1<p<∞; F is G-measurable and in D^{1,p}(Ω;X), where G is generated by the Poisson random measure.
theorem_cards.statement: F=E(F)+I(P_F(DF)); P_F(DF) is the unique adapted Y∈L_F^p(Ω;ν_p(R_+×J;X)) that represents F−E(F) through the Itô integral.
proof_steps: Construct P_F as the strong operator limit of partitionwise conditional expectations; uniform boundedness follows from ν_p-boundedness of conditional expectations, obtained from R-boundedness.

Use adjointness of D and δ, Theorem 5.10 identifying δ with the adapted Itô integral, and the duality identity for adapted integrals to prove φ=P_F(DF) whenever F=I(φ). Reduce general centered F by density to scalar cylindrical cases and use the scalar Poisson Clark–Ocone theorem; uniqueness follows from injectivity of I.

proof_source_ranges.scope: Projection construction, Lemma 6.5, and full proof of Theorem 6.6.

gaps: The proof invokes the scalar Clark–Ocone formula as an external cited result.
The representation applies to the stated Poisson Sobolev domain and natural Poisson σ-algebra, not arbitrary semimartingale decompositions.

constant_dependence.explicit: Type/cotype integral estimates depend on p,s and the martingale type/cotype constant of X. The UMD Itô equivalence depends on p and the UMD geometry of X. The convolution inequality additionally depends on the semigroup dilation bounds. The ν_p-bounded projection constants depend on p,X through UMD/R-boundedness. No dimension-free arbitrary-Banach constants are claimed.

endpoint_limits.exponents: Most type/cotype and UMD statements require p>1; Theorem 2.11 has a low range 1<p≤s (while Theorem 3.3’s printed low range includes p=1). UMD results require 1<p<∞.
endpoint_limits.intensity: All results use compensated Poisson random measures with deterministic σ-finite intensity. Small-cell moment comparison requires cell intensity ≤1, achieved by refining the simple-process partition.
endpoint_limits.filtration: The Clark–Ocone/Itô-divergence identification uses the natural Poisson filtration; the authors emphasize this in Remark 5.11.
endpoint_limits.space: Type/cotype inequalities are one-sided for general Banach X; UMD abstract isomorphism uses stochastic ν_p norm; explicit deterministic descriptions are provided only for particular spaces.

reusable_methods.method: Lexicographically order small-intensity Poisson cells so compensated cell increments times adapted coefficients become martingale differences; combine type/cotype with Poisson moment comparison.
reusable_methods.transfer: A candidate route for finite-increment moment/tail estimates when the target has deterministic-intensity Poisson cells and appropriate martingale geometry. It does not establish a compensator for a state-dependent jump process.

reusable_methods.method: Use UMD decoupling and a stochastic ν_p integrand norm to identify the closed Poisson Itô map; use conditional expectations to project onto adapted integrands.
reusable_methods.transfer: Can clarify the exact natural-filtration and domain conditions for jump-integral interfaces, but does not provide the J04-specific nonhomogeneous intensity or exit-settlement semantics.

reusable_methods.method: For stochastic convolutions, transfer a maximal integral bound through an isometric semigroup dilation.
reusable_methods.transfer: Applicable only after a valid dilation on a suitable type-s space has been supplied.
